cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Amazon ElastiCache is AWS's fully managed in-memory cache running Valkey, Redis OSS or Memcached. Put it in front of RDS, Aurora or DynamoDB for microsecond reads, typically with lazy loading and TTLs.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Serverless needs no sizing, scales automatically and bills per GB and ECPU; node-based clusters let you choose node types, shards and replicas. For HA use Valkey or Redis OSS with Multi-AZ and automatic failover. Choose Memcached for the simplest multi-threaded model; Valkey or Redis for rich types and replication.

questions.q: If ElastiCache fails over to a replica, can data be lost?
questions.a: Yes, with standard replication. It is asynchronous, so acknowledged writes not yet copied are lost.
Serverless scales automatically with no sizing; node-based gives control of node types, shards and replicas.

questions.q: What is a shard in Valkey or Redis OSS?
questions.a: One primary node plus up to five read replicas holding the same data.
